name: Allergy & immunology (category guide)
summary: Skin-prick / blood panels vs symptom-led work-ups — foreigner fee honesty, immunotherapy cost clocks, and when derm or ENT should lead instead.
body: Expat threads asking for a ‘full allergy panel’ often meet clinicians who test against symptoms, not a hundred-allergen buffet. Public hospital allergy clinics (e.g. NUH pathways) are cheaper for citizens/PRs; foreigners usually pay full fees, so private immunology / allergy clinics buy speed more than subsidy. Ask whether you are seeing an SMC-registered immunologist, a dermatologist for chronic urticaria, or an ENT for allergic rhinitis — the wrong door wastes cash. Immunotherapy (injection courses measured in years) is a budget decision, not a one-visit fix; get written package scope and drop-out fees. Food / drug challenge tests need controlled settings — mall ‘allergy screens’ are not the same product. Pair with paediatric allergy guides when the patient is a child, and with health-insurance schedules that often carve allergy testing thinly. This is a category guide, not a ranked clinic list.
